lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Make Characters Move
lesson.summary: Join command blocks so a sprite moves, grows and talks, then test the program.
learning_objectives: Change values and see the result
Test and fix a small program

standards.text: Create and debug simple programs; use logical reasoning to predict the behaviour of simple programs
Develop programs with sequences and simple loops, to express ideas or address a problem

success_criteria: I can say what a sprite and a block are
I can change a number and predict what happens
I can test a program and fix a bug
lesson.real_life: Making a cartoon on a tablet, or telling a robot toy where to go.

warm_up.prompt: Which key makes a capital letter?

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how do we make a character move?
blocks.say: Today we make a character move. Layla wants her cartoon cat to walk and talk.

blocks.alt: An orange and white cat sitting on a paved path looking up
blocks.caption: A real cat. Layla draws a cartoon cat from it.
blocks.credit: Photo by Louis Droege on Unsplash
blocks.say: This real cat inspired Layla. She turns it into a character on a screen.

blocks.text: Stop 1: A sprite is a picture you control

blocks.markdown: A **sprite** is a picture that a program can move.
blocks.say: A character on a screen is called a sprite. A sprite is a picture a program can move.

scenes.caption: The cat sprite.
scenes.say: Here is Layla's cat. It is a sprite on a green background.

scenes.caption: A garden background.
scenes.say: A background is the picture behind the sprite. This one is a garden.

scenes.caption: A program controls it.
scenes.say: The program tells the sprite what to do. The sprite cannot move alone.

question.hint: It is a picture you control.
question.explanation: A sprite is a character a program can move.

options.text: A cartoon cat on the screen

blocks.markdown: A **command block** tells the sprite to do one thing.
blocks.say: We give the sprite commands. Each command is a block. Blocks snap together in order.

blocks.alt: A wooden stacking toy with red, yellow, blue, orange, purple and green rings
blocks.caption: Rings go on in order, like blocks in a program.
blocks.credit: Photo by Tomáš Petz on Unsplash
blocks.say: The cat does the first block first. Then the next block. The order matters.

scenes.caption: Move 5 steps.
scenes.say: The first block says move five steps. The cat walks.

scenes.caption: Grow.
scenes.say: The next block says grow. The cat gets bigger.

scenes.caption: Meow.
scenes.say: The last block says meow. The program is a sequence.

question.prompt: What does a command block do?
question.explanation: Each block gives the sprite one job.

options.text: Makes the cat sleep for ever
Tells the sprite to do one thing

blocks.title: Layla's cartoon cat
blocks.transcript: Layla draws a cartoon cat. It is her sprite. She plans three boxes. Walk, grow, meow. She snaps blocks together in order. She runs it. The cat walks across the garden. The cat grows bigger. Next it should meow. Oh no. The cat turns the wrong way. That is a bug. Layla swaps one block. She runs it again. Now it walks, grows and meows. Layla shares it kindly.
blocks.caption: Layla joins blocks so her cat walks, grows and meows.

points: A sprite is a picture a program can move
Command blocks tell the sprite what to do
blocks.say: Let us remember. A sprite is a picture you control. Blocks tell it what to do, in order.

A block that tells a sprite to do one thing.
The picture behind the sprite.

blocks.markdown: Change the **number** in a block to change what happens.
blocks.say: A move block has a number. Move three steps goes a short way. Move five steps goes further.

scenes.caption: Move 3.
scenes.say: The block says move three steps. The cat walks a little.

scenes.caption: Move 5.
scenes.say: Change it to five. Now the cat walks further.

scenes.caption: Bigger means further.
scenes.say: A bigger number moves the sprite further.

blocks.title: Hop along
blocks.goal: Move the 6 hops of the cat across the garden. Each hop is one block.

question.prompt: A block says move 3. You change it to 6. What happens?
question.explanation: A bigger number moves the sprite further.

blocks.text: Stop 2: Each sprite has its own blocks

blocks.markdown: Each sprite has its own set of **blocks**.
blocks.say: Layla adds a dog. The dog has its own blocks. The cat's blocks do not move the dog.

scenes.caption: Two sets.
scenes.say: The cat has move blocks. The dog has turn blocks.

scenes.caption: Both act.
scenes.say: Run the program. The cat walks and the dog turns round.

scenes.caption: Own blocks.
scenes.say: Each sprite follows only its own blocks.

blocks.title: Make it walk
materials: A tablet with a blocks coding app
instructions: Pick a sprite and add a move block.
Change the number and run it. What changes?

blocks.say: Now you try. Ask a grown-up to open a blocks program on a tablet.

question.prompt: The cat's blocks also control the dog.
question.hint: Each sprite has its own blocks.
question.explanation: Each sprite follows only its own blocks.

points: Each sprite has its own blocks
blocks.say: Let us remember. Numbers change what blocks do. Each sprite has its own blocks.

terms.meaning: A value in a block, like 3 or 5.

mini_quiz.explanation: Turn changes the way it faces.

blocks.markdown: A **prediction** is a guess about what will happen.
blocks.say: Before we run a program, we predict. A prediction is a guess about what will happen.

scenes.caption: Predict.
scenes.say: The blocks say: move two, turn right, move two. Where will the cat go?

scenes.caption: Run.
scenes.say: Run it. The cat goes right, turns and goes down.

scenes.caption: Check.
scenes.say: Our prediction was right! If it is wrong, we learn.

question.explanation: A prediction is a guess before we run it.

options.text: A guess about what will happen

blocks.markdown: Play the memory game. Then look for a **bug**.
blocks.say: First a memory game. Then spot the bug in a program.

question.prompt: The cat should turn right but turns left. What is that?
question.hint: It is a mistake in the blocks.
question.explanation: A wrong turn block is a bug.

points: A bug is a mistake in the blocks
Run the program to test it
blocks.say: Let us remember. Predict first, then run. Fix any bug.

terms.meaning: A guess about what will happen.

blocks.markdown: **Design** first. Draw what each sprite will do.
blocks.say: Layla wants a short cartoon. A cat walks, grows and meows. First she draws a plan.

blocks.markdown: A plan has steps, like a story.
blocks.say: She draws three boxes. Box one: the cat walks. Box two: the cat grows. Box three: the cat meows.

blocks.title: Plan an animation
instructions: Draw three boxes. Show what happens in each.
Write which block each box needs.
Share your plan with a friend.
blocks.say: She writes which block goes with each box. The plan tells her what to build.

scenes.caption: Box 1: walk.
scenes.say: Box one shows the cat walking across the garden.

scenes.caption: Box 2: grow.
scenes.say: Box two shows the cat growing bigger.

scenes.caption: Box 3: meow.
scenes.say: Box three shows the cat saying meow. A plan saves time.

question.prompt: Put the animation steps in order.

blocks.markdown: **Test** your program. Then make it better.
blocks.say: Layla builds her program and runs it. The cat walks. But it turns the wrong way.

scenes.caption: A bug.
scenes.say: She runs the program. The cat walks. Then it spins the wrong way.

scenes.caption: Fix it.
scenes.say: She swaps the turn block to the right one. She runs it again.

scenes.caption: It works.
scenes.say: Now it works. She asks a friend for kind feedback.

blocks.markdown: Kind feedback says what is good and what could be better.
blocks.say: Her friend says, I like the meow. Maybe make the cat bigger.

question.prompt: What should you do after you build a program?

blocks.say: Let us remember. Plan, build, test and improve with kind feedback.

terms.meaning: A plan for what you will make.
Try it to see if it works.
Kind comments that help someone improve.
Make something better.
Steps drawn or written before you build.

mini_quiz.prompt: What do we do before building?

mini_quiz.explanation: Kind feedback names a good thing and a way to improve.
